labs.title: CSRF-protected contact form
labs.subtitle: A plain Form, validation, POST/redirect/GET and a safe email boundary.
labs.goal: Build a contact form that validates input, shows field errors and redirects only after success.
labs.scenario: A marketing page needs a contact form. It must reject malformed email addresses, require a message and never send twice on refresh.
tasks: Create `ContactForm` with name, email, topic, message and consent fields.
Use `request.POST or None` so GET renders an unbound form.
On valid POST, send via a small function and redirect.
acceptance: GET shows an empty form.
POST with a bad email shows an error and does not send.
Valid POST calls the email function once and redirects.
Refreshing the success page does not resend.
hints: Use `form.is_valid()` before touching `cleaned_data`.
`request.POST or None` avoids a bound empty form on GET.
A `Textarea` widget only changes HTML, not validation.
labs.explain: The form is the validation boundary. The view decides what success means. The redirect is what prevents duplicate sends on refresh.

labs.title: ModelForm CRUD with permissions
labs.subtitle: Create, edit and delete one object without trusting the URL.
labs.goal: Build create and update views with one ModelForm and an ownership check.
labs.scenario: A notes app lets each user edit only their own notes. The form should never expose the owner field.
labs.starter_code:
# models.py
class Note(models.Model):
    owner = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    body = models.TextField()

# forms.py
class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ["title", "body"]

# views.py
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)
    # TODO: ownership + form + save
tasks: Return 404 for another user's note, not 403 with data leakage.
acceptance: A user can create a note and is set as owner.
Edit only changes title/body.
Another user's note returns 404.
Invalid input re-renders with errors.
hints: Never put `owner` in `Meta.fields`.
`commit=False` lets you set server-controlled fields.
Filtering the queryset by owner is both authorization and a clean 404.
labs.explain: Authorization belongs in the queryset, not only in the template. If the object is not yours, it should not exist for this request.

labs.title: A custom inclusion tag
labs.subtitle: Reusable template markup with an explicit context.
labs.goal: Build an inclusion tag that renders a badge from a status value.
labs.scenario: Several templates need the same status pill. Copy-pasting it causes inconsistent labels and CSS.
tasks: Map `draft`, `published` and `archived` to label and CSS class.
Return only the context the partial needs.
Load and use the tag in a template.
acceptance: Known statuses render the expected label/class.
Unknown status does not crash.
The partial has no database queries.
The tag can be reused in two templates.
hints: A dictionary lookup is enough for three statuses.
Use a fallback label like “Unknown”.
Inclusion tags are for markup, not business logic.
labs.explain: The tag owns presentation, not permission or queries. Keeping the context small makes the partial easy to test and reuse.

labs.title: Transaction-safe stock decrement
labs.subtitle: Row locks, atomic updates and a deliberate failure path.
labs.goal: Prevent overselling when two requests decrement the same stock row.
labs.scenario: A checkout endpoint reads stock, creates an order and decrements stock. Two concurrent requests must not both succeed when only one item remains.
tasks: Return a conflict response without partial writes.
acceptance: A successful purchase creates one order and decrements once.
Zero stock returns 409 and creates no order.
Two simulated concurrent purchases cannot both take the last item.
An exception rolls back both order and stock changes.
hints: Lock the row before the stock check.
`select_for_update()` only helps inside a transaction.
A `F()` update is atomic but still needs a constraint/check for the full workflow.
labs.explain: The lock serializes the critical section. The recheck inside the transaction is what makes the decision safe; the update alone is not the whole workflow.

labs.title: Paginated search without N+1
labs.subtitle: Filtering, pagination and prefetching in one queryset.
labs.goal: Build a searchable, paginated product list that does not explode query count.
labs.scenario: A catalogue page filters by query and category, shows 20 products per page, and each product displays its category and tags.
tasks: Filter by `q` on name/description and by category.
Preserve query parameters in pagination links.
acceptance: Search and category filters combine.
Page 2 returns the next 20 objects.
The page executes a constant number of queries for 20 rows.
An empty search state is rendered.
hints: Use `Q(name__icontains=q) | Q(description__icontains=q)`.
`select_related` is for foreign keys; `prefetch_related` is for many-to-many.
Do not slice before `Paginator`.
labs.explain: The queryset is the contract: filter it, join what you know, prefetch what you render, and paginate the final result.

labs.title: A small DRF endpoint with validation
labs.subtitle: Serializer, permissions, pagination and an explicit response contract.
labs.goal: Expose a read/create API for notes owned by the authenticated user.
labs.scenario: A mobile client needs `GET /api/notes/` and `POST /api/notes/`, but must only see its own notes.
tasks: Add pagination and a stable ordering.
acceptance: Anonymous access is rejected.
A user sees only their own notes.
Creating a note sets the owner automatically.
The list is paginated and ordered.
hints: `IsAuthenticated` is the permission class.
Never trust an `owner` field from the client.
`ordering = ["-created_at"]` prevents unstable pagination.
labs.explain: The queryset is the authorization boundary. The serializer validates shape; `perform_create` owns server-controlled fields.

labs.title: Login, ownership and a safe 404
labs.subtitle: Protect a view and avoid leaking whether someone else's object exists.
labs.goal: Protect a document detail view and return 404 for objects the user cannot access.
labs.scenario: A private document URL must require login and must not reveal another user's document existence.
tasks: Add a test for anonymous and foreign access.
acceptance: Anonymous request redirects to login.
Owner sees the document.
Other user gets 404, not the document.
The test covers both cases.
hints: `login_required` can wrap the view or use `LoginRequiredMixin`.
`get_object_or_404(Document, pk=pk, owner=request.user)` is enough.
404 is both a security and a UX choice here.
labs.explain: Authentication answers “who are you”; authorization answers “which rows may you see”. The queryset filter implements the second.

labs.title: Validated file upload
labs.subtitle: Size, type, storage and a clean failure path.
labs.goal: Accept an avatar upload only when it is a small image, and store it safely.
labs.scenario: Users upload avatars. The server must reject oversized files and non-images before saving the model.
tasks: Reject files above 2 MB with a form error.
Use `ImageField`/Pillow validation for real image checks.
Store through the configured storage backend.
acceptance: A valid small image saves.
A non-image is rejected.
A file over 2 MB is rejected.
The error is attached to the image field.
hints: Check `image.size` in `clean_image()`.
The extension is not a security check.
Do not read the whole file into memory just to validate it.
labs.explain: Upload validation is a server rule, not a client hint. Storage is a boundary; the view should not care whether files live on disk or S3.

labs.title: Cached dashboard with invalidation
labs.subtitle: Cache the expensive read, invalidate on the write.
labs.goal: Cache a dashboard query for 60 seconds and invalidate it after a relevant write.
labs.scenario: A dashboard aggregates order totals. It is read constantly and changes only when an order is created.
tasks: Cache the aggregate under a stable key for 60 seconds.
Invalidate the key after creating an order.
Add a test that proves the second read does not hit the queryset.
acceptance: First request computes and caches.
Second request reads the cache.
Creating an order invalidates the cache.
Per-user data is never placed in a shared key.
hints: Use `cache.get` / `cache.set` / `cache.delete`.
A shared key must not include private user data.
Invalidate after the transaction commits if consistency matters.
labs.explain: A cache is a second source of truth. The write path must own invalidation, and the key must match the sharing boundary.

labs.title: A useful management command
labs.subtitle: Arguments, output, dry-run and a safe default.
labs.goal: Build a command that finds inactive users and can delete them only with `--confirm`.
labs.scenario: An admin wants a repeatable cleanup command. The default must be a dry run; deletion needs an explicit flag.
labs.starter_code:
# management/commands/cleanup_users.py
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Remove inactive users"

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        # TODO: filter, report, confirm
        pass
acceptance: Without `--confirm`, no rows are deleted.
`--days 30` filters by `last_login`.
With `--confirm`, only matching rows are deleted.
Output states what would happen or what happened.
hints: Use `parser.add_argument`.
A dry run is the safe default.
Print the count before deleting.
labs.solution:
from datetime import timedelta
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.utils import timezone

class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Remove inactive users"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=90)
        parser.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true")

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        cutoff = timezone.now() - timedelta(days=options["days"])
        users = get_user_model().objects.filter(last_login__lt=cutoff)
        count = users.count()
        if not options["confirm"]:
            self.stdout.write(f"Would delete {count} users. Re-run with --confirm.")
            return
        users.delete()
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(f"Deleted {count} users."))
labs.explain: Commands are production code. A dry run, an explicit confirmation and a summary make destructive operations reviewable.
